title: Fennel's Brave Boat Ride
markdown:
Coco the cockapoo’s tail did a happy little thump-thump-thump against the soft, sun-warmed grass. It was a happy sound, like a little drumbeat. Her friend, Fennel the frog, sat on his favourite lily pad by the edge of the big, shimmering pond. He looked a little bit wobbly. His big, thoughtful eyes were wide, and his little froggy fingers were clasped tightly.

“Oh, Coco,” Fennel whispered. His voice was like the softest rustle of leaves in a gentle breeze. “The blackberries on Sunbeam Island look so plump and purple today. I can see them sparkling from here!” He pointed a slightly trembling webbed hand towards a small, sunny island in the middle of the pond. “But… the pond looks so very, very big.”

Coco padded closer. The sweet, damp smell of dewdrops on clover tickled her nose. Sunbeam Island was famous for its blackberries. People said they tasted like sunshine. They were also very, very juicy, like a summer rain shower. Fennel was a little bit nervous about going on the water. He liked his lily pad; it stayed put, his safe, floaty home.

“Don’t worry, Fennel!” Coco said, her voice as warm and comforting as a soft, happy sigh. She nudged a large, bright yellow leaf that had drifted down from the big oak tree. It was shaped like a little boat and floated perfectly on the pond’s surface, which mirrored the sky like a fallen piece of blue. “It’s a sunshine boat! We can sail on it right to the island!”

Fennel looked at the yellow leaf. It did look cheerful, like a piece of captured sunshine. But then he looked at the pond again. It shimmered and spread out. His little froggy knees felt like they might do a jig all on their own, a nervous, shaky jig. “A… a boat?” he croaked. The word came out like a tiny puff of air. He felt a little flutter in his tummy, like a tiny moth. This is worry, he thought.

“Yes! A super-duper leaf boat,” Coco explained, her tail giving another hopeful thump. It was a steady, reassuring sound. “It will carry us right to the yummiest, juiciest blackberries ever. If you like, you can hold onto my fur. It’s very soft and warm, like a fluffy cloud.” Fennel imagined the plump, purple blackberries, glistening like tiny jewels. He imagined Coco’s warm, soft fur.

He took a deep, wobbly breath. “Okay, Coco,” he said, his voice a tiny bit louder this time, a brave little croak. “Let’s try.”

With Coco’s gentle encouragement, Fennel carefully hopped onto the sunshine boat. It dipped slightly, making him feel a little fluttery inside. Then, Coco, with her paws placed very carefully, hopped on beside him. The bright yellow leaf bobbed and dipped, and Fennel’s legs did a tiny tremble, like a leaf in a very small breeze. But Coco’s fur was just as warm and soft as she had promised, and her happy, panting breath was a steady rhythm beside him.

“We’re floating!” Fennel whispered, his eyes still a little wide, but also filled with a new feeling: wonder. The pond water rippled gently around them, like a soft, blue blanket being tucked around their boat. A little breeze, smelling of damp earth and sweet, wild clover, began to tickle their noses. It was a whisper-soft breeze, and it made the yellow leaf boat dance and sway just a little, like it was doing a gentle waltz on the water. The yellow leaf dipped, smelling of damp earth and sweet clover, its texture rough and papery beneath his tiny webbed feet, and the sight of the water shimmering so far below made his tummy do a flip.

“Whee!” chirped Coco, her voice full of delight. “The wind is helping us fly!” The sunbeams were warm on Fennel’s back, chasing away any lingering wobbly feelings. The breeze wasn’t trying to push them anywhere scary; it just made their journey feel like a happy, gentle sway.

Soon, with a soft little nudge, the sunshine boat bumped gently against the sandy shore of Sunbeam Island. And there they were! The bushes were heavy with the biggest, purplest blackberries Fennel had ever seen. They shimmered in the sunlight, so plump and ready they looked like tiny, edible jewels. The air itself smelled deliciously sweet.

Fennel hopped off the leaf boat, his legs still a tiny bit wobbly, but his heart feeling much bigger and braver than it had before. He carefully picked a blackberry, its skin smooth and cool. He popped it into his mouth. Oh! It was bursting with sweet, juicy flavour, a tiny explosion of sunshine and sweetness, even better than he had imagined. He looked at Coco, who was already happily munching on another blackberry, her tail wagging so fast it was a golden blur.

“You did it, Fennel!” Coco said, her mouth full of berry goodness, her voice muffled but happy. “You were so brave! And these blackberries are the bestest ever!”

Fennel smiled, a real, happy froggy smile that spread all the way to his ears. He had been a little bit nervous, yes. But he had also been brave. And now he was here, eating the most delicious blackberries in the whole wide world, with his best friend right by his side. The sunshine boat bobbled gently in the shallow water, a perfect, happy yellow against the clear blue. Fennel looked out at the pond, and it didn’t seem quite so big anymore. It looked like a pathway to fun, and the little yellow leaf boat had carried him there. He knew that trying new things could lead to the sweetest, most wonderful adventures.
